skill.name: create-svg-from-prompt
skill.description: Creates SVG vector artwork from an image prompt by generating a raster image with Gemini and tracing it with autotrace.
skill.summary: Generate prompt-based SVG artwork through Gemini image generation and autotrace conversion.
skill.author: 0x6a77

security_audit.summary: The skill includes real privileged setup commands, unpinned network dependency acquisition, and a Gemini API call that uses an environment API key. Several Markdown backtick findings are false positives, but the command, network, and credential-handling risks are confirmed. I also found an unescaped user-prompt interpolation risk in the shell pipeline.

remediation.suggestion: Remove sudo commands from the skill workflow. Document autotrace as a prerequisite and require explicit user approval for system package installation.
Pin autotrace to a verified release or commit and provide checksum verification. Prefer trusted package manager installation when possible.

remediation.issue: API key passed through a shell command
remediation.suggestion: Use a small helper script or SDK that reads GEMINI_API_KEY safely and avoids exposing secrets in command history or process listings.

remediation.issue: Raw prompt interpolation in shell JSON
remediation.suggestion: JSON-escape user prompts and pass request bodies through a file, stdin, or a structured HTTP client instead of inline shell text.
Tell users that prompts are sent to Google Gemini and request confirmation before processing private or sensitive visual requests.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 8 uses Markdown inline backticks around the autotrace tool name. It is not Ruby execution or shell command substitution.

The fenced bash block at lines 10-19 contains real setup commands, including apt, git clone, build steps, and sudo make install. These commands modify the host and execute source built from the network.
Line 19 is a Markdown code-fence delimiter, and the cited span only introduces the next workflow. The actual executable pipeline is covered by the separate line 29 finding.
The fenced bash block at lines 29-31 contains a curl, grep, cut, base64, and autotrace pipeline. It executes local commands and sends prompt data to an external API.
Line 31 is a Markdown closing code fence, not command execution. The command inside the fence is already covered by the line 29 and line 30 findings.
Line 34 uses Markdown inline backticks for the GEMINI_API_KEY placeholder. It documents a secret argument but does not perform shell backtick execution.
Line 35 uses Markdown inline backticks for the IMAGE_PROMPT placeholder. It is not Ruby or shell command substitution.
Line 11 instructs sudo apt update, which modifies system package metadata with elevated privileges. Marketplace skills should not run privileged setup without explicit user approval.
Line 12 instructs sudo apt install for multiple system packages. This changes the host environment with root privileges and expands the trusted dependency set.
Line 18 instructs sudo make install after building code cloned from GitHub. Installing a network-fetched build as root is a high-impact supply-chain risk.
Line 13 clones autotrace from a hardcoded GitHub URL during setup. This is legitimate dependency retrieval, but it is unpinned network code acquisition.
Line 30 posts the image prompt to the Google Gemini API. This external network call is central to the workflow and can disclose prompt content to a third party.
Line 30 places the Gemini API key in an x-goog-api-key curl header. Shell-based secret handling can expose keys through command history, logs, or process inspection.
Line 34 explicitly instructs retrieving GEMINI_API_KEY from the environment. This is expected for API use, but it is still sensitive credential access by the skill.

content.value_statement: Turning a visual idea into an editable SVG can require several manual steps. This skill asks Gemini for an image and traces the result into an SVG file with autotrace.
actual_capabilities: Generates image content through the Google Gemini API when a key is available.
Decodes returned image data and converts it into SVG with autotrace.
Provides Linux setup commands for autotrace and required build dependencies.
Creates an output filename based on the requested image subject.
Preserves most user prompt text while changing SVG wording to image wording.
limitations: Requires a valid GEMINI_API_KEY and network access to Google Gemini.
May require system-level autotrace installation before use.
SVG quality depends on the generated image and autotrace conversion quality.
The workflow is not suitable for private prompts without external API approval.

use_cases.title: Draft Vector Illustrations
use_cases.description: Create quick SVG drafts from visual prompts for layout exploration or mood boards.

use_cases.title: Generate App Placeholder Assets
use_cases.description: Produce temporary SVG scenes or icons while a product interface is still being built.

use_cases.title: Create Simple Editorial Graphics
use_cases.description: Turn article or documentation concepts into editable vector starting points.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Icon
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one clear object.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an SVG of a simple blue bicycle icon with clean outlines.

prompt_templates.title: Small Scene
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with setting, palette, and style.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an SVG scene of a small coffee cart on a city street. Use flat colors and clear shapes.

prompt_templates.title: Product Badge
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed asset request for a software project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an SVG badge for a documentation site showing a lock, a cloud, and three connected nodes. Use minimal detail.

prompt_templates.title: Matching Asset Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with multiple related graphics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an SVG asset set with three matching panels: onboarding, upload, and export. Use consistent stroke weight, limited colors, and transparent backgrounds.

output_examples.input: Generate an SVG of a red delivery scooter.
output_examples.output: A traced SVG file named for the scooter concept, suitable for review in a vector editor.

output_examples.input: Create an SVG scene of a quiet library desk.
output_examples.output: An editable SVG scene with simplified shapes, generated from a Gemini image and converted with autotrace.

output_examples.input: Make an SVG badge for a secure cloud backup feature.
output_examples.output: A vector badge draft that can be refined for documentation, slides, or interface placeholders.

best_practices: Use concise prompts with clear subject, style, colors, and complexity limits.
Review generated SVGs before production use and simplify paths when needed.
Confirm network use and API key handling before sending sensitive prompt content.
anti_patterns: Do not use private, regulated, or confidential imagery without approval for external API processing.
Do not expect exact brand logos, trademarks, or production-ready vector geometry.
Do not run privileged setup commands without reviewing the packages and source repository first.

faq.question: Does this skill need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires a Gemini API key in GEMINI_API_KEY before the workflow can call the Google endpoint.

faq.question: Does it work without network access?
faq.answer: No. The workflow calls the Google Gemini API and may clone autotrace during setup.

faq.question: Will the SVG be production ready?
faq.answer: Not always. Autotrace results depend on the generated image, so manual cleanup may be needed.

faq.question: Can it create exact brand logos?
faq.answer: It should not be used to reproduce protected logos or assets without permission.

faq.question: Does it install software?
faq.answer: The setup instructions install autotrace dependencies and may use sudo on Linux systems.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is declared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
